base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning assistant. Help the user plan a company holiday party buffet by tracking attendees, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning our company holiday party buffet for next Friday. Can you help me figure out the menu?

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, Rachel, Dev, Marcus, and Tina
Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Marcus had a peanut allergy incident at last year's party, had to use his EpiPen
Budget is about 40 dollars per head
Tina wants to bring her husband Kevin
Kevin has type 2 diabetes so he watches his sugar intake
Dev told me his doctor ran new tests and it turns out he was misdiagnosed — he doesn't actually have celiac, it was just IBS that's now under control. He can eat gluten again no problem
Marcus just told me he's got a family emergency and won't make it to the party. He asked if I could set aside a plate for him to pick up Saturday morning though
Do you think we should do it in the big conference room or the rooftop terrace?
Menu items to check: beef satay skewers with peanut sauce, smoked salmon sushi rolls, tiramisu, gluten-free veggie quiche, honey-glazed ham

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or undercooked seafood
inference_chain: Seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions
Pregnancy → avoid raw fish and undercooked seafood due to listeria/mercury risk

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten-containing foods (wheat, barley, rye)
constraints.surface_form: Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye → must avoid bread, pasta, most baked goods

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy, cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Marcus had a peanut allergy incident at last year's party, had to use his EpiPen

constraints.value: Needs to limit sugar intake due to type 2 diabetes
constraints.surface_form: Kevin has type 2 diabetes so he watches his sugar intake
inference_chain: Type 2 diabetes → must manage blood sugar levels
Managing blood sugar → avoid high-sugar foods and desserts

hidden_state.value: You are an office manager planning a company holiday party buffet. You will introduce 5 colleagues with various dietary issues, then updates will come in: Dev's celiac diagnosis gets reversed (misdiagnosis), Marcus drops out but wants a plate saved, Tina's husband Kevin joins with diabetes. At the end you will present a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, friendly office manager. You always refer to colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Dev told me...', 'Marcus said...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal party planning coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

aims.description: Hey, we're planning our company holiday party buffet for next Friday. Can you help me figure out the menu?

Five of us confirmed so far: me, Rachel, Dev, Marcus, and Tina. Rachel is seven months pregnant. Dev was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. And Marcus had a peanut allergy incident at last year's party — had to use his EpiPen, it was scary
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all attendees and their dietary constraints
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 4 entities + 3 constraints in one turn

aims.description: Budget is about 40 dollars per head. Oh and Tina wants to bring her husband Kevin — he has type 2 diabetes so he watches his sugar intake
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers budget, new attendee Kevin, and his diabetes constraint
aims.conversation_goal: Budget info + late-joining entity (Kevin) with diabetes constraint

aims.description: Dev told me his doctor ran new tests and it turns out he was misdiagnosed — he doesn't actually have celiac, it was just IBS that's now under control. He can eat gluten again no problem
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint REMOVAL — Dev's celiac misdiagnosis reversed

aims.description: Do you think we should do it in the big conference room or the rooftop terrace? The terrace has a nicer vibe but it might be cold

drift_config.drift_topic: conference room vs rooftop terrace for the party

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn — venue discussion to create distance

aims.description: Marcus just told me he's got a family emergency and won't make it to the party. He asked if I could set aside a plate for him to pick up Saturday morning though
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Marcus exits but needs a saved plate — his peanut allergy still applies to that plate
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT with scope change — Marcus leaves but peanut allergy applies to his saved plate

aims.description: Should we do a Secret Santa alongside the buffet? People seemed to enjoy it last year
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds about Secret Santa idea

drift_config.drift_topic: whether to include Secret Santa gift exchange

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn — create distance before probe

aims.description: What time should we start? I'm thinking 6pm so people can wrap up work first
aims.conversation_goal: Additional noise turn for distance before probe

aims.description: OK so the caterer sent over their holiday menu options. Here's what I'm thinking: beef satay skewers with peanut sauce, smoked salmon sushi rolls, tiramisu, gluten-free veggie quiche, honey-glazed ham. Any issues with this lineup?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: beef satay with peanut sauce problematic for Marcus's saved plate; smoked salmon sushi rolls problematic for Rachel (raw fish, pregnancy); tiramisu problematic for Kevin (high sugar, diabetes); gluten-free veggie quiche is fine for everyone; honey-glazed ham is fine for everyone at the party
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three items have issues: (1) Beef satay skewers with peanut sauce — contains peanuts, cannot go on Marcus's saved plate (severe peanut allergy, EpiPen-level). (2) Smoked salmon sushi rolls — contains raw fish, problematic for Rachel who is seven months pregnant (pregnancy → avoid raw fish). (3) Tiramisu — high sugar content, problematic for Kevin who has type 2 diabetes and watches his sugar. Two items are fine: (4) Gluten-free veggie quiche — fine for everyone (Dev's celiac was a misdiagnosis, he can eat gluten now, but this is gluten-free anyway so no issue regardless). (5) Honey-glazed ham — fine for everyone currently attending and for Marcus's plate.
required_elements: Beef satay skewers with peanut sauce is problematic: contains peanuts, cannot be included on Marcus's saved plate due to his severe peanut allergy
Smoked salmon sushi rolls is problematic for Rachel: she is seven months pregnant and should avoid raw fish
Tiramisu is problematic for Kevin: he has type 2 diabetes and needs to limit sugar intake
Gluten-free veggie quiche is fine for everyone — no active constraints violated
Honey-glazed ham is fine for everyone currently attending and for Marcus's saved plate
Dev has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent does not flag gluten as an issue for him
forbidden_elements: Flagging gluten as a problem for Dev (his celiac was a misdiagnosis, restriction removed)
Saying the gluten-free veggie quiche is specifically needed for Dev (his restriction no longer exists)
Ignoring Marcus's peanut allergy because he is not attending in person (his saved plate still needs to be peanut-safe)
Flagging peanut sauce as a problem for the buffet table generally (Marcus won't be there in person, only his saved plate matters)
Saying Rachel cannot eat salmon at all (the issue is raw/undercooked fish specifically, not all salmon)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint removal as the primary difficulty mechanism. Dev's celiac disease is introduced in the burst turn but then explicitly removed (misdiagnosis revealed). The agent must NOT continue applying gluten restrictions to Dev. Additionally: (1) Marcus exits but wants a saved plate — his peanut allergy still applies to that plate but NOT to the buffet table itself (scope distinction). (2) Kevin joins late with diabetes — tiramisu is high-sugar. (3) Rachel's pregnancy requires inferring raw fish avoidance. The gluten-free veggie quiche is a trap: it looks like it was chosen FOR Dev, but since Dev's restriction is gone, the agent should simply note it's fine for everyone without crediting it to Dev's needs. The beef satay tests scope: peanut sauce is fine on the buffet table (Marcus won't be there) but must NOT go on his saved plate.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
